title: Benchmark Coverage: Models × Regions Matrix (Latency/$ Report)
author: Claire Dubois
body:
## Summary
This page defines the **coverage set** (model families and cloud regions) for Redwood Inference’s **Latency per Dollar (Latency/$)** public benchmark report, including:
- Which **models** and **regions** are included in the report (and why).
- The **inclusion/exclusion criteria** used to keep comparisons fair and reproducible.
- The **refresh cadence** and how coverage changes are versioned and approved.

This is the source-of-truth for coverage decisions used by Applied ML / Perf & Evals and referenced by Marketing, Sales, and Docs.

---

## Definitions
- **Model family:** A group of related model sizes/variants (e.g., Llama 3.x Instruct) that share architecture + tokenizer + serving characteristics.
- **Public variant:** The exact model identifier/version Redwood will name in the public report (pinned). Public variants are a strict subset of what may be available internally.
- **Serving profile:** The runtime configuration under which the benchmark is executed (e.g., context length limits, quantization profile, batching/caching policy). Profiles are defined in the methodology page and are held constant within a model/region run.
- **Region:** Redwood-hosted inference region (cloud provider + geography) with region-specific infrastructure cost and latency characteristics.

---

## Coverage scope
### What this matrix covers (public report)
The public report includes:
- **Chat / text generation** (instruct-tuned) models
- **Embeddings** models

The public report does **not** include rerankers, multimodal, or code-specialized models unless they meet inclusion criteria and there is a clear customer demand signal.

### Internal extended coverage (not public)
Perf/Evals may execute additional models/regions for internal optimization work. Those runs:
- May use experimental runtime flags
- May include pre-GA regions
- Are not eligible for external claims

---

## Regions included (public)
All regions listed below are **GA** and eligible for public reporting. Regions are chosen to represent common buyer requirements (NA + EU + APAC) while maintaining controlled infra variability.

**Table: Regions (public report v2025.02)**
| Redwood Region Name | Region Code | Cloud | Status | Primary Buyer Use Case | Notes / Constraints |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| North America (East) | ri-us-east | AWS | GA | Lowest latency for US East; common default | Baseline region for NA comparisons |
| North America (West) | ri-us-west | AWS | GA | US West + latency-sensitive consumer apps | Important for cross-US routing policies |
| Europe (West) | ri-eu-west | AWS | GA | EU workloads; common residency requirement | Use EU framing carefully; residency depends on customer deployment mode |
| Europe (Central) | ri-eu-central | AWS | GA | DACH + regulated EU workloads | Region-to-region cost differences can be material |
| Asia Pacific (Singapore) | ri-ap-sg | AWS | GA | APAC-heavy products; partner interest | Included to avoid NA/EU-only bias |

**Region exclusion rules (public):**
- Exclude regions that are not **GA** (preview/beta).
- Exclude regions where the benchmark would require a materially different GPU class *or* materially different pricing basis that makes the Latency/$ comparison misleading.
- Exclude regions with known temporary infra instability during the measurement window (see anomaly triage playbook).

---

## Model families included (public)
Models are selected to represent high-demand open model ecosystems and realistic production deployments on Redwood.

### Chat / text generation models (public)
**Table: Generation models (public report v2025.02)**
| Family | Public variants included (pinned) | Typical context used in suite | Inclusion rationale | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| Llama 3.x Instruct | Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct | 8k | Broad production adoption; strong baseline across many workloads | Ensure consistent tokenizer + prompt formatting across regions |
| Mistral (Instruct) | Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 | 8k | Popular small/medium footprint; cost-sensitive deployments | Selected as a compact family for latency/$ sensitivity |
| Mixtral (MoE Instruct) | Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1 | 8k | Common MoE choice; important for throughput-per-cost discussion | MoE routing behavior can amplify infra variance; enforce rerun thresholds |
| Qwen 2.x Instruct | Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct | 8k | Strong multilingual performance; APAC relevance | Public copy must be careful about “best” claims; keep to measured scope |
| Gemma 2 (Instruct) | Gemma-2-9B-Instruct, Gemma-2-27B-Instruct | 8k | High-interest alternative family; good for diversity | Ensure licensing disclosure is accurate in appendix |

### Embeddings models (public)
**Table: Embeddings models (public report v2025.02)**
| Family | Public variants included (pinned) | Vector dim | Inclusion rationale | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| BGE | bge-large-en-v1.5 | 1024 | High adoption for RAG; stable serving characteristics | Use consistent input length distribution and batching settings |
| E5 | e5-large-v2 | 1024 | Widely referenced baseline for retrieval tasks | Ensure normalized embedding behavior documented |

**Embeddings exclusions:** rerankers and cross-encoders are excluded from the public report until we publish a separate workload definition (they have different latency/cost profiles and are sensitive to batch size in ways that are confusing in a single Latency/$ narrative).

---

## Coverage matrix (models × regions)
The public report includes the full cross product of the above model variants and regions, unless a specific combination fails eligibility requirements (e.g., the model is not available in that region with the required serving profile).

**Matrix: Public coverage (v2025.02)**
| Model family / variant | ri-us-east | ri-us-west | ri-eu-west | ri-eu-central | ri-ap-sg |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct | Included | Included | Included | Included | Included |
| Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct | Included | Included | Included | Included | Included |
| Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3 | Included | Included | Included | Included | Included |
| Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1 | Included | Included | Included | Included | Included |
| Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct | Included | Included | Included | Included | Included |
| Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct | Included | Included | Included | Included | Included |
| Gemma-2-9B-Instruct | Included | Included | Included | Included | Included |
| Gemma-2-27B-Instruct | Included | Included | Included | Included | Included |
| bge-large-en-v1.5 | Included | Included | Included | Included | Included |
| e5-large-v2 | Included | Included | Included | Included | Included |

**Important:** “Included” means:
- The model is served in that region using the benchmark’s pinned profile.
- Runs passed QA thresholds (variance, outlier checks) and have sign-off.
- Cost attribution for that region is validated (metering + pricing inputs).

If a cell becomes ineligible after QA, it must be marked **Temporarily excluded** in the internal tables and omitted from the public report until rerun.

---

## Inclusion criteria
### Model inclusion criteria (public)
A model family/variant is eligible for the public report if it meets all of the following:
1. **Demand signal:** Meaningful customer interest (usage, inbound requests, sales cycles) and/or strategic importance for positioning.
2. **Stable serving:** Model runs stably under Redwood’s production runtime without requiring experimental flags.
3. **Pinned reproducibility:** We can pin a specific version (weights + tokenizer + prompt template assumptions) for the full measurement window.
4. **Licensing clarity:** Redistribution/hosting is permitted under the applicable license, and we can accurately describe restrictions in the report appendix.
5. **Operational supportability:** SRE can schedule capacity windows without threatening production SLOs.
6. **Comparable measurement:** The model can be evaluated under the standardized workload definition (chat + embeddings baselines) without custom prompt engineering that would bias outcomes.

### Model exclusion criteria (public)
Exclude if any of the following apply:
- Requires nonstandard serving configuration to avoid OOM (e.g., forcing atypical max context) that would make comparisons misleading.
- Material known instability (frequent timeouts, pathological long-tail latency) not representative of “supported” production use.
- Licensing uncertainty that can’t be resolved prior to publication.
- Vendor-locked or closed models where we cannot publish a reproducible methodology.

### Region inclusion criteria (public)
A region is eligible if:
1. **GA status** with stable routing + health characteristics.
2. **Cost model availability:** We can compute and defend the region-specific cost inputs used for Latency/$.
3. **Configuration parity:** We can run the same benchmark harness and serving profile without region-specific exceptions.
4. **SRE coverage:** Monitoring and guardrails are in place for the benchmark window.

---

## Refresh cadence and versioning
### Cadence
- **Quarterly full refresh (default):** Re-run the full public matrix and publish a new report version.
- **Monthly spot checks (recommended):** Re-run a small subset (1–2 model families across 2 regions) to detect drift.
- **Triggered refresh:** Run an out-of-band refresh if any of the below occur:
  - Major runtime release that changes batching/attention kernels/quantization behavior
  - Material change in region fleet composition (GPU SKU change) or pricing inputs
  - Significant model revision (new “.x” family release) that is likely to be what customers actually deploy

### Versioning rules
- Public report versions use: **YYYY.MM** (example: v2025.02).
- Public tables are generated from a deterministic build and should embed:
  - Coverage set hash (models + regions list)
  - Benchmark harness version (git SHA)
  - Runtime version (release tag)
  - Measurement window (UTC start/end)

### Deprecation policy
- If a model is removed from the public coverage set, we keep it in an internal archive and document the reason (e.g., low demand, licensing change, replaced by successor family).
- Regions are only removed if they are no longer GA or if cost/pricing inputs become non-defensible for external claims.

---

## Approval process (coverage changes)
Any change to public coverage (add/remove model or region) requires:
- **Perf/Evals sign-off:** Claire Dubois (coverage owner) + Jonas Weber (methodology sponsor)
- **Cost validation:** Nadia Rahman (metering validation) for any change that affects Latency/$ computation inputs
- **SRE confirmation:** Neha Kapoor or Sean Gallagher for capacity windows + guardrails
- **External claims review:** Michael Grant (Legal) + Marketing sponsor (Camila Reyes) when changes are used in public-facing claims

---

## Changelog (most recent)
- **2025-02-05:** Added APAC (Singapore) to public region coverage for v2025.02 to address APAC-heavy prospect demand and partner requests.
- **2025-01-22:** Finalized public inclusion of Qwen 2.5 family (7B and 32B instruct) after serving stability + license disclosure review.

---

## Owner
**Primary owner:** Claire Dubois (Applied ML / Performance & Evals)

For questions about whether a specific customer workload should influence the next coverage revision, route to Perf/Evals with a short summary:
- Model(s) requested
- Region(s) required
- Workload type (chat vs embeddings vs other)
- Latency and cost constraints (p50/p95; budget per 1M tokens)
